home_story_1: Two months ago I read the blog post “{post}” by Stepan Parunashvili about turning an iPhone into a dumbphone with Apple Configurator. I tried it. The setup was fine; the effort is a part of why it holds. But that setup had some serious problems.
home_story_2: The App Store was off, so nothing updated. I couldn't log in to my bank app. The web was an allow list, so I could not even scan a QR menu at a restaurant. The configuration part is done via Apple Configurator manually by clicking buttons. I realized using Apple Configurator isn't even necessary. So I built a guide that keeps the App Store on, blocks the apps even if they're installed, blocks their URLs, and leaves the rest of the phone alone.
home_story_3: I met a lot of people lately. Per my observations, most of people's problems come down to not being able to do hard things. When I check their screen time I mostly saw 6 hours and more.
home_story_4: People do anything to escape the hard work. And having an infinite amusement machine on their fingertips makes this a thousand times easier.
home_story_5: I think I finally fixed this for myself and I wanted to turn my expertise into a non-profit social awareness project.
home_story_6: That is the whole reason this site exists. If more people try blocking these distracting apps, we could learn more, experiment more and share more.
home_story_7: I used the time I got from Instagram reels to build this website as the ultimate example.
home_story_8: We should get better at protecting ourselves and our next generations from a system built to farm attention.
home_story_9: It is not only the hours. It is what the hours do. You stop doing hard things. You stop getting better at anything. The muscle goes soft and you become a cog. I wanted a way out that does not depend on willpower, because mine runs out by afternoon like everyone else's.
home_story_10: Most people will close this tab. That is fine. This is for the ones who will be glad they found it, the way I was glad I found that blog post.
home_how_body: Two ways to take the feeds off your iPhone for good.
home_how_app_lead: Keeps everything on your iPhone. Nothing is erased.
home_how_app_body: Plug the iPhone in, click, wait. The app copies it, flips one flag in the copy and restores it, so it comes back supervised, with the feed apps and their sites blocked by a profile that cannot be removed.
home_how_app_fail: If supervision fails, your license key stays unused.
home_how_diy_lead: Erases your iPhone. You set it up again from a backup afterwards.
home_how_diy_body: You supervise the iPhone with Apple Configurator, Apple's own Mac app, and follow the guide one step at a time.
home_computer_body: The same feeds live on the computer. {extension} pulls them out of X, YouTube and Instagram in the browser, and leaves the accounts where you can work. It is free and open.
home_faq_supervision_desc: A device mode Apple built for schools and companies. A supervised iPhone accepts settings a normal one refuses: hiding apps, and a profile that cannot be removed. Everything else about the phone stays the same.
home_faq_choice_desc: The app keeps everything on the iPhone and costs $29 per supervision. Doing it yourself is free, but Apple Configurator erases the iPhone first, so you set it up again from a backup.
home_faq_data_desc: Not with the app. It copies your iPhone to your Mac, flips one flag in the copy, then restores it to the same phone, so photos, messages and logins stay. Apps re-download, and an encrypted copy keeps your saved passwords, Health and keychain, so fewer of them ask you to sign in again. The App Store stays on and only the apps you list disappear. Doing it yourself erases the iPhone, so back it up first.
home_faq_fail_desc: Your license key stays unused. If supervision does not go through, you can use the same key again on the next try.
home_faq_see_term: Can anyone see or track my phone?
home_faq_see_desc: No. Supervision is a flag, not a connection; remote control needs an MDM server, and you enrol in none. The profile is a fixed, signed file: once installed, nobody can change it or read anything back.
home_faq_undo_desc: Only by erasing the iPhone. Supervision is enforced by iOS, so the app cannot take it back off; you can add restrictions any time, but cannot loosen or remove one without erasing. Erase from Settings, then restore from iCloud or your local backup.
home_faq_mac_desc: Yes, for one afternoon. The app needs Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or newer. Borrow a friend's Mac: the app runs from Downloads and nothing stays on it. The phone needs no Mac afterwards.
home_faq_other_platforms_desc: iPhone only today, from a Mac. Windows support is planned, since the same copy works through iTunes. Android needs a different build, a small device-owner app, and is planned too.
home_faq_who_desc: Mert Duzgun, a developer in Antalya. The code is public, and the profile is signed with my Apple developer certificate.
gen_footer_not_apple: A {builder} awareness project. Not affiliated with Apple.
ext_privacy_lead: The attention awareness extension hides feeds with CSS. It collects nothing.
ext_privacy_stores_body: Your switches (on or off per site) and the custom CSS rules you write, in the browser's extension storage.
ext_privacy_stores_sync: If you are signed into your browser, the browser may sync that storage across your devices. Nothing else.
ext_privacy_sends_body: Nothing. No analytics, no crash reports, no remote code, no network requests of its own.
ext_privacy_sees_body: The pages on x.com, youtube.com and instagram.com, only to inject CSS.
ext_privacy_sees_custom: If you add a custom rule for another site, the browser asks you once for access to that site. The extension then injects your CSS there and nothing more.
ext_privacy_source_body: The code is public at {repo}, and the rules are plain CSS files you can read.
guide_description: The free, do-it-yourself way to a supervised, feed-free iPhone: Apple Configurator on a Mac, then a profile that blocks the feeds. It erases the iPhone.
guide_title: Supervise your iPhone yourself, for free
guide_lead: The do-it-yourself way to a feed-free iPhone. Apple Configurator on a Mac supervises the phone, then a profile blocks the apps and sites you choose.
guide_erase_body: Supervising with Apple Configurator wipes the phone, and you set it up again as new. Back it up first, to iCloud or to your Mac in Finder, so you have a way back.
guide_erase_app: Want to keep everything on it? The {app} supervises it without erasing, for $29 per supervision.
guide_need_mac: A Mac, and a cable for your iPhone.
guide_need_passwords: Your iPhone passcode and your Apple Account password.
guide_step_backup_icloud: To iCloud: on the iPhone, Settings > your name > iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now.
guide_step_backup_finder: To your Mac: plug the iPhone in, open Finder, select the iPhone, then General > Back Up Now.
guide_step_backup_note: Keep this backup. It is your way back if you change your mind.
guide_step_erase_body: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings. It asks for your passcode and your Apple Account password, which also turns off Find My.
guide_step_erase_hello: When the iPhone restarts, leave it on the Hello screen.
guide_step_configurator_body: Get {configurator} from the Mac App Store. It is free and made by Apple. Open it and click Get Started.
guide_step_prepare_connect: Plug the iPhone into the Mac. When it shows up in Configurator, right-click it and choose Prepare.
guide_step_prepare_manual: Choose “Manual Configuration” and tick “Supervise devices”. Leave “Add to Apple School Manager or Apple Business” unticked.
guide_step_prepare_skip: If it asks about device management, choose “Do not enroll in Device Management”. If it asks you to sign in to Apple School Manager or Apple Business, click Skip.
guide_step_prepare_org: For the organization, enter your own name. You are an organization of one.
guide_step_prepare_setup: For Setup Assistant, choose “Don't show any of these steps”, then click Prepare.
guide_step_prepare_done: Configurator erases the iPhone once more and brings it back supervised.
guide_step_setup_title: Set it up as a new iPhone
guide_step_setup_no_restore: Do not restore the backup from step 1. A backup from before supervision takes supervision off again.
guide_step_setup_account: In Settings, set a passcode and Face ID, and sign in with your Apple Account. What you keep in iCloud comes back on its own, like photos, contacts, messages and passwords.
guide_step_setup_apps: Then install the apps you need from the App Store.
guide_step_setup_check: The top of Settings now says the iPhone is supervised.
guide_step_build_body: Open the {builder}, pick the apps and sites to block, and download the profile. It is free.
guide_step_build_by_hand: Configurator can also build a profile by hand, under File > New Profile, if you would rather set every option yourself.
guide_step_install_body: Drag the profile onto the iPhone in Configurator, or right-click the iPhone and choose Add > Profiles. A supervised iPhone takes it without asking.
guide_step_install_done: The apps you blocked disappear, and their sites stop loading.
guide_step_install_more: Forgot something? Build another profile and add it the same way. It adds to the one already there.
guide_undo_body: Erase the iPhone from Settings: General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings. That takes supervision and every profile off. Then restore the backup from step 1.
build_apps_body: It starts with the feed apps people lose the most hours to. Search the App Store to add more.
build_description: Pick the apps and websites to block on a supervised iPhone, then download a signed profile. Free and open source.
build_guide: Not supervised yet? {guide} shows how to get there.
build_install_1: On a Mac, open Apple Configurator and connect the supervised iPhone with a cable.
build_install_2: Select the iPhone, click Add, then Profiles, and choose the file you downloaded.
build_install_3: If the iPhone asks, open Settings and tap Install.
build_install_phone: Downloading on the iPhone itself? Tap Allow, then go to Settings > Profile Downloaded > Install.
build_lead: Pick the apps and websites to block, then download a signed profile. It goes on a supervised iPhone.
build_mac: The {mac} also installs profiles for free on any supervised iPhone.
build_stack_note: Every download is a new profile. A second one adds to the first and cannot loosen or replace it.
build_web_allow_body: Safari opens only the sites on this list and blocks everything else.
build_web_deny_body: Hiding an app leaves its website open, so every blocked app adds its sites here. Untick a site to leave it open.
gen_allow_app_store_help: Turning it off also stops app updates; banks and airlines break. Blocking apps by name is usually better.
gen_app_search_error: The App Store search did not answer. Try again in a moment.
gen_apps_empty: No apps blocked yet. Search above to add some.
gen_install_note: Blocked apps still download from the App Store, but they stay hidden and will not open.
gen_permanent_check: I understand this profile is permanent: it cannot be changed or removed without erasing the iPhone
gen_sign_unavailable: Signing is not available right now
gen_trial_check: Trial mode: I can remove this profile later
gen_trial_help: Off by default. A trial profile can be removed in Settings. Turn it off and download again when you are ready to commit.
gen_web_private_browsing: Allow private tabs and clearing history
